questions.q: What structural capability do Customer Community Plus and Partner Community license tiers add that a plain Customer Community license (and sharing sets) does not have?
options: Unlimited storage for portal users
A role hierarchy scoped to the external account itself, giving differentiated visibility within the same external account rather than treating every user at that account identically
The ability to disable the organization-wide default entirely
Automatic Named Credential creation for portal users
questions.explain: Account-scoped role hierarchy is a structurally different mechanism from a sharing set -- it adds a visibility dimension (differentiation within the same account) that sharing sets don't provide at all.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe account-scoped role hierarchy as structurally different from a sharing set, rather than just a bigger version of one?
options: A sharing set grants access based on matching the user's account to the record's account, treating every user at that account identically; account-scoped role hierarchy instead differentiates visibility among users within the same account
Sharing sets and account-scoped role hierarchy are actually the same mechanism with different names
Account-scoped role hierarchy only applies to internal employees, never external users
Sharing sets can only be used with the Partner Community license tier
questions.explain: The two mechanisms solve different problems: a sharing set answers 'does this user's account match this record's account,' while role hierarchy answers 'who among this account's own users should see more than others.'

questions.q: Why is a large, deep external account role hierarchy a performance consideration, not just a licensing question?
options: Because external accounts have a hard cap of ten portal users regardless of license tier
Because Salesforce's sharing-recalculation engine has to process every record-visibility implication of a role or ownership change, and that recalculation cost scales with the hierarchy's complexity
Because deeper hierarchies automatically trigger more Apex callouts
Because role hierarchies cannot be used with Named Credentials
questions.explain: Sharing recalculation cost grows with hierarchy complexity -- a hierarchy deeper than actual visibility requirements justify adds recalculation cost without adding real access-control value.

questions.q: What is the specific, concrete trigger this lesson gives for deciding a portal design needs to move to a higher license tier?
options: Any customer with more than three portal users automatically needs the higher tier

Whether any customer actually needs differentiated visibility among their own users -- some seeing more of that account's records than others -- as opposed to every user being functionally interchangeable
Whether the customer's industry is considered 'enterprise' by Doverfield's sales team
Whether the customer has ever logged a support case
questions.explain: The trigger is a named requirement (differentiated internal visibility), not a size or industry heuristic -- a customer whose users are interchangeable doesn't need the higher tier regardless of how large the account is.

questions.q: Why does this lesson warn against modeling a customer's full internal org chart as a deep account-scoped role hierarchy 'just because the data is available'?
options: Because external account hierarchies are technically impossible to build deeper than two levels
Because a hierarchy deeper than the actual visibility requirements justify adds sharing-recalculation cost without adding any real access-control value
Because Salesforce prohibits external role hierarchies from exceeding the internal employee hierarchy's depth
Because org charts are considered confidential and cannot be modeled in Salesforce
questions.explain: The lesson's point is that hierarchy depth should be driven by actual access-control requirements, not by how much organizational data happens to be available to model -- unnecessary depth is pure recalculation overhead.
